idiom_name: class with the core concept as members + extension functions for additional behaviour (same-file rule)
implementation_notes: Kotlin keeps the concept as a class and splits where its behaviour lives: member functions for what defines the type, extension functions for additional functionality computed on top of the concept's public API, which the official API guidelines recommend for library design. The coding conventions add the contour rule: extensions relevant to all clients belong in the same file as the class, client-specific ones next to their client, and files created merely to collect extensions are discouraged. Extensions are dispatched statically and cannot be overridden, so anything participating in inheritance or needing private state stays a member.
pitfalls: Extension functions see only the public API: an operation that needs internal state must be a member, and forcing it into an extension leads to relaxed visibility that widens the contour.
Extensions are not virtual and a member with the same signature always wins, so behaviour designed for overriding stays a member.
Top-level extension files unrelated to their receiver scatter the concept; keep them beside the class or the client they serve.
